p1.original: 11.1 我们的行为通常要符合社会情境，当面对不熟悉、不明确的情境时，我们会参考他人的行为。
p1.en: 11.1 Our behaviour is usually in accordance with social circumstances, and when faced with unfamiliar and unclear circumstances, we refer to the behaviour of others.

p2.original: 11.2 他人的行为和我们如何解释他人在社会背景中的行为，这二者都会影响我们对他人的看法。
p2.en: 11.2 The behaviour of others and how we interpret the behaviour of others in the social context influence our perception of others.

p3.original: 11.3 社会系统会影响情境，而情境会影响行为。通过理解社会系统，我们就可以学习如何优化它，同时消除其所造成的负面影响。
p3.en: 11.3 Social systems influence situations that affect behaviour. By understanding the social system, we can learn how to optimize it while eliminating its negative effects.

p4.original: 比尔在阅读周日报纸时，得知他所在的小镇的一所著名大学正在招募年龄为20～50岁的成年男性参加一项心理学实验，该实验旨在提高人们的记忆力。比尔自愿参加了这项有趣且有价值的实验，并且他还将获得一小笔报酬。比尔到达大学的实验室后，研究人员热情地接待了他，并且向他介绍了名叫道格拉斯的另一位被试。实验者穿着醒目的实验室工作服，向被试介绍这项研究的目的，即检测当人们犯错误时是否可以通过惩罚来改善其学习和记忆。他说：“对正确反应的正强化是提高动物和人类的记忆力的关键。我们现在想检测对不正确反应的惩罚是否也能达到类似的效果。”这两个被试通过抽签确定谁扮演老师，谁扮演学生，扮演哪个角色看似并不重要。
p4.en: When reading the Sunday newspaper, Bill learned that a well-known university in his town was recruiting adult males aged 20 to 50 to participate in a psychological experiment designed to enhance people's memory. Bill volunteered to participate in this interesting and valuable experiment, and he will receive a small reward. Upon his arrival at the university's laboratory, the researchers warmly received him and informed him of another trial, Douglas. The experimenter, wearing a visible laboratory worksuit, introduced the purpose of the study, which is to test whether people can improve their learning and memory by punishing them for their mistakes. He said, “The right response is being strengthened and is key to improving the memory of animals and humans. We now want to test whether penalties that respond to incorrect reactions can have a similar effect. It does not seem important that the two were tried by drawing lots to determine who was the teacher and who was the student and which role.

p5.original: 这项任务很简单：比尔将扮演“老师”的角色，并给“学生”道格拉斯提供一组成对的单词，道格拉斯需要在给定的时间内对这些单词进行记忆。每当学生回答正确时，老师都会给他一个口头奖励，如“很棒”或“正确”。当学生回答错误时，老师要按一下电击设备上的操作杆，它会立即发出电击来惩罚学生。
p5.en: The task is simple: Bill will play the role of “teacher” and provide “student” Douglas with a pair of words that Douglas needs to remember within a given time. Every time a student answers correctly, the teacher gives him an oral reward, such as “very good” or “right”. When the student answers the error, the teacher presses the operating pole on the electroshock device, and it sends an immediate electric shock to punish the student.

p6.original: 电击设备一共有30个开关，最低电压为15伏，以15伏为一级强度逐渐增加，最高为450伏。控制面板显示了每个开关所对应的电压以及与其相关的描述。例如，第25级（375伏）的开关上标记着“危险，电击水平强烈”，而在第29级和第30级（435伏和450伏）处，控制面板只标注了代表不祥征兆的“×××”。实验者指出，每当学生犯错时，老师必须按下比上一次电击水平更高的开关。
p6.en: A total of 30 switches with a minimum voltage of 15 volts and a gradual increase in the first-level strength of 15 volts to a maximum of 450 volts. The control panel displays the charge of each switch and its associated description. For example, the switch for class 25 (375 V) is marked as “hazardous, highly electroshocked”, while in classes 29 and 30 (435 V and 450 V), the control panel is marked only as “xxx” representing an ominous omen. The experimenter pointed out that whenever a student made a mistake, the teacher had to press a switch at a higher level than the previous electric shock.

p7.original: 学生道格拉斯进入了相邻的房间，他的手臂被紧紧地绑着，腕部安装着电极。如果学生犯了错，隔壁房间中的电击设备会电击学生的手腕。道格拉斯提到他的心脏有一些小毛病，希望电击不会对他造成太大的损害。实验者向他保证，虽然电击很强烈，但不会对他造成任何永久性的伤害。实验过程中实验人员会站在比尔的旁边，比尔可以通过对讲机与道格拉斯进行对话并提出测试问题。
p7.en: The student, Douglas, entered the adjacent room, his arms were tied tight and electrodes were installed on his wrist. If the student makes a mistake, the electroshock device in the next room will electroshock the student's wrist. Douglas mentioned that his heart had some small problems and hoped that the shock would not cause him too much damage. The experimenter assured him that, although the electric shock was strong, it would not cause him any permanent harm. During the experiment, the experimenter would stand next to Bill, who could use a walkie-talkie to talk to Douglas and ask questions about testing.

p8.original: 实验之初，道格拉斯表现出色，并得到了比尔的称赞。然而，很快他开始出现错误，比尔立即按下那些电击开关。随着道格拉斯犯的错误越来越多，电击水平也越来越高，他开始抱怨电击对他造成了伤害。在电压处于75伏时，他呻吟了一声，在第10级电压150伏时，道格拉斯表示他受不了了，要求终止实验。比尔焦急地看向实验者，实验者点了点头并示意他必须继续。随着电击强度的增加，道格拉斯的尖叫声也随之提高，他提醒实验者自己患有心脏病。现在比尔真的心烦意乱，他对实验者说：“先生，如果那个人的身体出了状况，谁负责呢？”“我将负全责，现在请继续进行你的任务，老师。”实验者的话打消了比尔的顾虑。随着实验次数越来越多，电击水平越来越高，隔壁房间也传来更刺耳的尖叫声。比尔很犹豫并询问实验者是否还要继续，但实验者坚决主张他别无选择，必须继续。
p8.en: At the beginning of the experiment, Douglas had done well and received Bill's praise. However, soon after he began to make a mistake, Bill immediately pressed those shock switches. As Douglas made more mistakes and the level of electric shocks increased, he began to complain about the damage caused to him by electric shocks. When the voltage was 75 volts, he moaned, and when the voltage of level 10 was 150 volts, Douglas said he could not stand it and demanded that the experiment be terminated. Bill was anxious to look at the experimenter, who noded and suggested that he must continue. As the intensity of the electric shock increased, so did Douglas's screams, which he reminded the experimenter of a heart attack. Now Bill is really upset, and he says to the experimenter, "Sir, who's responsible if that person's body is in a state of health? “I will take full responsibility, and now please continue your mission, teacher. "The words of the experimenters dispelled Bill's concerns. As the number of experiments increased and the level of electric shocks increased, the next room also heard more loud screams. Bill hesitated and asked if the experimenter was going to continue, but the experimenter insisted that he had no choice but to continue.

p9.original: 当电压达到300伏时，道格拉斯要求退出实验，并大声地喊道自己有心脏病。比尔受够了。他提出异议：“先生，我不能再伤害他了，我拒绝继续。”实验者十分冷漠地让比尔继续进行实验，因为他签署了完成实验程序的合同。
p9.en: When the voltage reached 300 volts, Douglas asked to withdraw from the experiment and shouted out that he had a heart attack. Bill's had enough. He objected: “Sir, I can't hurt him any more, I refuse to continue. “The experimenter left Bill to continue the experiment with great indifference, as he signed a contract to complete the experimental procedure.

p10.original: 比尔不情愿地继续对道格拉斯的错误施加惩罚。当电压达到330伏时，他听见了尖叫声和“砰”的重物撞击声，然后电击室变得沉寂。比尔说：“他没有回应了，应该有人去看看他是否安好。”但是实验者仍不为所动：“如果学生没有在规定时间内回答问题，即漏答，也需要受到与回答错误相同的惩罚。这是规则，你必须服从。”
p10.en: Bill reluctantly continued to punish Douglas for his mistakes. When the voltage reached 330 volts, he heard screams and bangs of heavy objects, and then the electric shock chamber became silent. Bill said, "He's not responding. Someone should see if he's okay. However, the experimenter remains still unmoved: “If the student fails to answer the questions within the prescribed time, that is, to omit, he is also subject to the same punishment as the error in answering. That's the rule, you have to obey.

p11.original: 当比尔继续给予下一个级别的电击时，学生道格拉斯毫无反应。比尔大声地抱怨说，在这种情况下继续进行实验是不合乎情理的。但是，他说的话无法撼动实验者，他无法从这难以意料、令人沮丧的困境中退出。相反，比尔被告知必须要遵守规则，因为作为老师，他的工作就是不断地提出测试题目并对学生的错误施加电击，即使这意味着要一直提高电压，直到450伏。比尔不停地抱怨，但也不断地按着越来越高的电击开关，一直到最高级别的电击！
p11.en: As Bill continued to give the next level of electric shock, the student Douglas did not react. Bill complained loudly that it would not be reasonable to continue the experiment in such circumstances. However, his words could not shake the experimenter and he could not withdraw from this unexpected and frustrating dilemma. On the contrary, Bill was told that the rules had to be followed, because, as a teacher, his job was to constantly raise the subject of tests and to electric shocks to students ' mistakes, even if that meant increasing the voltage until 450 volts. Bill's been complaining, but he's been pushing up and down to the highest level!

p12.original: 如果在该实验中你是比尔，你会怎么做？在什么电击级别下你会坚定地拒绝继续进行？大多数人都认为，我们会提出异议，违抗实验者的指令并离开实验室。你永远都不会因为几美元出卖自己的良知，对吗？谁会违背自己的良知，盲目服从权威的命令，去伤害无辜的人呢？也许只有精神病患者会。许多精神科医生预测只有1%的美国公民会提高电压到最大级别，这是美国的精神病患者所占的百分比。但他们大错特错！
p12.en: If you were Bill in that experiment, what would you do? What level of electroshock would you firmly refuse to continue? Most people think we're going to object, disobey the tester's instructions and leave the lab. You'll never sell your conscience for a few dollars, will you? Who, against their conscience, blindly obeys the authority to harm innocent people? Maybe only the mentally ill will. Many psychiatrists predict that only 1 per cent of United States citizens will increase their voltage to the highest level, which is the percentage of the United States ' mental illness. But they're so wrong!

p13.original: 该实验其实是由一位年轻的社会心理学家斯坦利·米尔格拉姆（Stanley Milgram）于1963年在康涅狄格州纽黑文（New Haven，Connecticut）的耶鲁大学（Yale University）进行的，当时他是一位新来的助理教授。他测试了来自各行各业的500多名普通公民（没有学生），发现每三位“老师”中就有两位（65%）会把电压提高到最高的450伏。大多数人在此过程中都会提出抗议，但仍会选择服从权威，对“学生”施加他们认为可能致命的电击。需要补充说明的是，学生实际上是实验者的助手，他们事先接受过训练，扮演了一个中年被试的角色。在实验中“学生”并没有遭受电击，只是他们的表现让“老师”误以为真。你将在本章中详细了解与米尔格拉姆的实验相关的内容，但现在让我们看一下这个实验所揭露出的人性本质。我们还将进一步了解40名精神科医生为什么会预测错误。
p13.en: The experiment was actually carried out in 1963 by Stanley Milgram, a young social psychologist, at Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut, when he was a new assistant professor. He tested more than 500 ordinary citizens (no students) from all walks of life and found that two out of three “teachers” (65 per cent) would raise the voltage to a maximum of 450 volts. Most of them protest in this process, but they still choose to submit to authority and impose electric shocks on “students”, which they believe may be fatal. It should be added that students are actually assistants to the experiment, who have been trained in advance and have played a mid-year test role. The “students” were not subjected to electric shocks in the experiment, but their performance made the “teachers” mistakenly believe that they were real. You're going to get a detailed look at what's related to the Mirgram experiment, but let's look at the human nature that this experiment reveals. We will also know more about why 40 psychiatrists are making mistakes.

p14.en: This chapter considers the following topics:

p15.original: 为什么普通人会像米尔格拉姆的电击实验中的被试那样伤害他人？
p15.en: Why would ordinary people hurt people the way they were tried in Mirgram's electroshock experiment?

p16.original: 同样重要的还有，尽管多数人表现出了完全的服从，但仍有少数人拒绝服从这种不公正的权威。在大多数有权威规则的实验和现实生活中，大多数人都会选择遵循、遵从、服从。但是，总有10%～30%的少数人会反抗。这让我们不禁思考，为什么某些人会逆流而上并付出他们的时间和精力去帮助陷入苦难的人，甚至做出英勇的行为？
p16.en: Equally important is the fact that, despite the complete obedience shown by the majority, there are still a few who refuse to obey this unjust authority. In most experiments and real life where there are authoritative rules, most people choose to follow, obey and obey. However, a minority of 10-30 per cent would resist. This leads us to wonder why some people go back and give their time and energy to help those in need, and even to commit heroic acts.

p17.original: 是什么使社会心理学与众不同

p18.original: 社会心理学（social psychology）是一个研究个体与个体之间如何相互影响的领域。当我们了解到除了服从权威之类的实验的负面结论外，还有许多社会心理学研究会带来好消息时，可能会感到欣慰。社会心理学还探索因人类聚集而产生的友谊和亲密关系，以及合作和冲突解决等。在本章中，通过学习社会心理学，你将了解个体与他人的互动是如何影响人们的思想、情感、知觉、动机和行为的。简而言之，你会发现三个核心主题（见图11-1）。
p18.en: Social psychology is an area of research on how individuals interact with each other. We may be pleased to learn that, in addition to the negative conclusions of experiments such as obedience to authority, there are many sociopsychological studies that will bring good news. Social psychology also explores friendship and intimate relations resulting from human gathering, as well as cooperation and conflict resolution. In this chapter, by studying social psychology, you will learn how the interaction of individuals with others affects people's thoughts, emotions, consciousness, motivations and behaviour. In short, you will find three core themes (see figure 11-1).

p19.original: 图11-1 社会心理学的三个核心主题
p19.en: Figure 11-1 Three core themes of social psychology

p20.original: 注：社会对我们的行为的影响来自外部情境、内部心理过程及我们所生活的广泛社会系统。
p20.en: Note: Social influence on our behaviour comes from external circumstances, internal psychological processes and the broad social system in which we live.

p21.original: 社会心理学家试图理解社会背景下的行为。广义地讲，谢夫林（Sherif，1981）认为社会背景（social context）既包括他人的真实、想象或象征性的存在，也包括人与人之间发生的活动和互动，还包括行为发生的环境，以及在特定环境下约束行为的期望和社会规范。社会心理学家渴望了解人与环境之间的相互作用，个体性格特征如何影响其在社会环境中的行为，以及它们又如何受到社会情境因素的影响。简而言之，即个体会如何影响情境，而特定的情境又会怎样影响这些个体？当然，社会心理学的主要研究内容还包括群体行为，如团队合作、从众、群体偏见和恐怖主义。社会心理学家认为，通过了解引发消极社会行为的过程和机制，可以找到积极的干预措施来预防或改变这种行为。
p21.en: Social psychologists try to understand behaviour in the social context. In a broad sense, Sherif, 1981 considers social context to encompass both the real, imaginary or symbolic existence of others, as well as the activities and interactions that occur between people, the circumstances in which the conduct occurs, and the expectations and social norms that bind behaviour in a given context. Social psychologists are eager to understand how people interact with the environment, how individual characteristics influence their behaviour in the social environment, and how they are influenced by social circumstances. In short, how can individuals influence situations, and how can particular situations affect them? Of course, the main study of social psychology also includes group behaviour, such as teamwork, socialism, group prejudice and terrorism. Social psychologists believe that positive interventions can be found to prevent or change negative social behaviour by understanding the processes and mechanisms that trigger it.

p22.original: 最重要的是，就像米尔格拉姆的电击实验一样，服从性研究强调了社会情境对我们行为的影响力。这是过去50年来社会心理学研究中出现的一个核心主题。
p22.en: Most importantly, as in Mirgram's electroshock experiment, the subjectivity study emphasizes the influence of social circumstances on our behaviour. This is a central theme that has emerged in the social psychology studies of the past 50 years.

p23.original: 但心理学家们知道，尽管情境具有强大的影响力，但它不仅仅指我们所应对的客观现实。当我们在一间房间里时，除了房间的物理尺寸、形状和颜色可能会影响我们在房间中的行为方式外，我们对情境所做的主观解释，即根据情境对我们的意义而产生的个人知觉也会影响我们的行为方式。因此，同一个物理环境对人们产生的影响可能因人而异，并且随着时间的变化，我们的体验也有所不同。个人建构的主观社会现实是社会心理学的第二个核心主题。我们必须理解这个充满期望和感性的世界，从而了解在友谊和亲密关系建立过程中的吸引力，以及暴力、偏见和歧视背后的排斥力。
p23.en: But psychologists know that, despite the powerful influence of the situation, it is not just about the objective reality we face. When we are in one room, in addition to the physical size, shape and colour of the room, which may affect the way we behave in the room, our subjective interpretation of the situation, that is, the sense of perception that comes to us in the context of the situation, can also affect the way we behave. Thus, the impact of the same physical environment on people may vary from person to person, and over time, we experience different experiences. The subjective social reality of individual construction is the second core theme of social psychology. We must understand this world, full of expectations and feelings, in order to understand the appeal of friendship and intimacy and the forces of exclusion behind violence, prejudice and discrimination.

p24.original: 社会心理学中的第三个核心主题探讨的是哪些人或事物创造并延续了社会情境，这些情境不仅包括监狱、帮派、邪教、刑讯中心，还包括其他积极的情境，如大学、志愿者组织、夏令营，以及影响人类行为的许多其他情境等。首先，我们将确定我们的研究重心：去强调各种情境影响我们的思维、感觉和行为的方式。其次，我们拓宽视角，强调系统在创建、延续和解释各种生活情境（无论好坏）中的重要性。发生欺凌行为的教室是一种情境，也就是行为的背景，而系统是学校的行政管理及其政策和程序。我们还将看到社会心理学家如何通过实验来改变情境，从而改变主观社会现实，进而改善人类的生存状况。这是许多社会心理学家的崇高理想，他们努力工作、致力于在许多领域中实现这一目标。理想情况下，社会心理学研究的应用目标是利用所获得的知识来改善人类的处境。
p24.en: The third core theme of social psychology is the creation and continuation of social situations involving not only prisons, gangs, cults, torture centres, but also other positive situations, such as universities, volunteer organizations, summer camps and many other situations affecting human behaviour. First, we will determine the focus of our research: to highlight the ways in which situations affect our thinking, feelings and behaviour. Secondly, we have broadened our perspective to emphasize the importance of the system in creating, sustaining and interpreting the various life situations, both good and bad. Classrooms where bullying occurs are a situation, that is, the context of behaviour, and the system is the administration of schools and their policies and procedures. We will also see how social psychologists can experiment to change the situation, thereby changing subjective social realities and thus improving the survival of humankind. This is the noble ideal of many social psychologists who work hard and are committed to achieving it in many areas. Ideally, the application of psychosocial research is aimed at using the knowledge gained to improve the human condition.
